How to remove metadata from a video (MP4 and MOV)

A video from your phone or from an AI generator can carry where it was recorded, which device or app made it, and a provenance record saying it was AI-generated. Here is what an MP4 or MOV contains and how to strip it without losing quality.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 5 min read

Open IA Cleaner

What metadata a video file contains

  • Location: iPhone and Android videos usually store the GPS coordinates where they were recorded.
  • Device and software: make, model, iOS or Android version, and the app or encoder that exported the file.
  • Dates of recording and editing.
  • XMP: editing history from apps such as Premiere Pro or CapCut.
  • C2PA / Content Credentials: a signed record that AI video tools and some editors add, often saying the video was generated or edited with AI. TikTok, Instagram and YouTube can read it.

How to remove video metadata with IA Cleaner

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Video.
  2. Drop your MP4, MOV or M4V. On a phone, tap the drop zone and pick the video from your gallery.
  3. Check the report: location, device data, XMP and Content Credentials are listed, and the box What the original reveals shows any tool, author or edit history found.
  4. Click Download clean video.

The video is cleaned losslessly: the metadata boxes are removed and the file structure is rebuilt, but no frame is re-encoded, so quality and size stay the same. Nothing is uploaded — even large videos are processed in your browser.

What stays in the file

  • The basic technical data every player needs (resolution, duration, codec) and the container’s internal creation time.
  • Anything visible in the picture or audible in the sound, including visible watermarks and burned-in captions.
  • Invisible watermarks embedded in the frames themselves, such as Google’s SynthID. Those are not metadata.

Other formats such as WebM, MKV or AVI are not supported yet. If you need them, export to MP4 first.

Other ways

  • ffmpeg: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -map_metadata -1 -c copy out.mp4 removes most global metadata without re-encoding, but can leave per-track data and does not always remove C2PA boxes.
  • Re-exporting from a video editor usually drops the original metadata but re-encodes the video and adds the editor’s own.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In videos (MP4, MOV) it identifies and removes recording location, device and app data, XMP and C2PA Content Credentials, without re-encoding a single frame. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
